pathway.title: Dorman Products, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage, liquidity and maturities are the strongest part of the credit. Total debt of USD 440.7 million is 1.28x last-twelve-months EBITDA and net debt of USD 273.7 million is 0.79x; EBITDA is derived because the issuer reports none, and excluding the USD 56.7 million Heavy Duty goodwill write-off leverage is 1.10x. Liquidity is USD 965.9 million, being cash of USD 167.0 million and USD 798.9 million of undrawn revolver, and the first maturity is the revolver in June 2031, followed by the USD 450.0 million notes in June 2034. The creditor consequence is that refinancing is not a near-term risk. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 26; calculation P1; calculation P2; calculation P3; calculation P22

Cash-flow durability is adequate, not strong, because free cash flow is volatile and the latest figure is flattered. Free cash flow was USD 191.6 million in 2024, USD 75.7 million in 2025 after a USD 250.4 million inventory build, and USD 269.2 million over the last twelve months, which includes USD 99.7 million of tariff refunds and a USD 177.6 million inventory release in nine months. Through the three years 2023 to 2025 it averaged USD 144.03 million, 44% of EBITDA, and covered the annual coupon of USD 28.13 million 5.12 times; excluding the refunds, last-twelve-months conversion is 49%. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 28; calculation P5; calculation P6; calculation P7; calculation P8; calculation P9; calculation P22

Business diversification is the weakest dimension. Light Duty is 79.43% of sales and 91.57% of segment profit, two customers take about 40% of sales and the four largest owe 78% of receivables, so a price or volume decision by one account reaches the segment that carries the debt. Heavy Duty earns 1.35% of segment profit and Specialty Vehicle, bought for USD 509.8 million, adds little cushion. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 79, 80, 95; calculation P15

The receivable programs are a second dependency of the same size as liquidity. USD 970.9 million of receivables would otherwise be outstanding, which is 1.01 times liquidity, and the financial institutions that run the programs can modify or terminate them; counting the receivables as debt-like funding lifts leverage to 3.57x. The programs also cost USD 50.7 million over the last twelve months, 1.80 times the annual note coupon, so they are a larger financing cost than the notes. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation P10; calculation P11; calculation P12; calculation P22

Margin stability is average because tariff timing moves earnings by several percentage points. The Light Duty segment margin rose from 12.80% in 2023 to 20.53% in 2025 and was 18.5% in the third quarter of 2026 against 23.7% a year earlier, while the group gross margin fell by 500 bp to 39.4%, because tariff costs are capitalised in inventory and price rises lead cost recognition. Earnings therefore depend on how fast the company passes tariff costs to customers who press for lower prices. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 20, 21, 23; calculation P16; calculation P17

Refinancing capacity is strong but its documents are not in the set. The June 2026 refinancing placed USD 450.0 million of 6.25% notes and extended the revolver to 2031, and the notes had a fair value of 96.76% of principal at the end of September 2026. Ranking, the security of the notes and covenant headroom are not established, so the view rests on maturity dates, liquidity and leverage. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 12, 26; calculation P14; Source readiness (CP-0)

Financial policy is the swing factor and is rated average. There is no dividend, but repurchases of USD 113.8 million in nine months 2026 took 83.66% of free cash flow excluding refunds, with USD 348.3 million of authorisation left, and the limits that the new documents place on them are not known. Business & governance rates the sponsor and governance risk medium. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 12, 28; calculation P19

The primary downside path is a tariff-led margin squeeze on Light Duty with pressure on the receivable programs. If the Light Duty margin fell back to its 2023 level of 12.80%, segment profit would fall by USD 130.74 million, EBITDA would be USD 214.05 million and total debt to EBITDA 2.06x, still below the 2.14x of 2023 and with 7.61 times coverage of the coupon; the larger risk is a withdrawal of the programs, which would need slightly more than all of today's liquidity. Both are bounds, not forecasts. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation P2; calculation P10; calculation P18; calculation P22

cells.text: Dorman Products, Inc. (Nasdaq: DORM), a Pennsylvania corporation with its headquarters in Colmar, Pennsylvania. The filings are for the consolidated group; no parent, sponsor or separate borrower is stated.

Management describes the company as one of the leading suppliers of replacement and upgrade parts for the motor vehicle aftermarket: passenger cars, light, medium and heavy trucks, and specialty vehicles such as UTVs and ATVs. About 144,000 distinct parts were marketed at 2025-12-31, and the company estimates a total addressable market of over USD 165 billion.

Net sales to aftermarket retailers (including their online platforms), dealers and wholesale distributors, recognised at a point in time on purchase orders of one year or less. About 76% of 2025 products were sold under brands the company owns; the rest were private label, other brands or bulk.
Light Duty 79.43%, Heavy Duty 10.92% and Specialty Vehicle 9.65% of USD 2,130.32 million (calculation N1).
Light Duty 91.57%, Heavy Duty 1.35% and Specialty Vehicle 7.08% of USD 379.28 million of segment income from operations (calculation N2); segment margins 20.53%, 2.20% and 13.05% (calculation N3).

About 9,000 active accounts at 2025-12-31. Two customers each exceeded 10% of 2025 net sales and together accounted for about 40% (39% in 2024; three customers and 44% in 2023); their sales are in Light Duty. Long-term agreements typically carry no purchase commitment.
More than 400 suppliers, none above 10% of purchases. About 38% of 2025 purchases came from suppliers in China and about 77% from outside the United States; purchase prices are set in U.S. dollars.
92.30% of 2025 net sales went to U.S. customers (USD 1,966.33 million of USD 2,130.32 million); the rest went mainly to Canada and Mexico.
38 warehouse and office facilities in the United States, Canada, China, Taiwan and India, of which five are owned; 3,871 employees, none under a collective bargaining agreement.

Customer-sponsored programs let the company sell receivables without recourse at Term SOFR-based discounts: USD 1,387.8 million were sold in 2025 (65.15% of net sales) and USD 843.6 million in nine months 2026 (51.59%), at a cost of USD 36.1 million. USD 970.9 million of further receivables would otherwise have been outstanding at 2026-09-26.
Provision for customer credits was USD 404.2 million in 2025 (18.97% of net sales); accrued customer rebates and returns were USD 197.4 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 182.6 million at 2026-09-26.

Nine months 2026 net sales were USD 1,635.09 million, up 2.68%. Management language, 2026-10-26: full-year 2026 net sales growth of 2% to 3% and adjusted diluted EPS of USD 8.50 to USD 8.70, excluding tariff changes after 2026-10-26.

runs.text: Strengths. Leverage and liquidity come first: total debt of USD 440.7 million is 1.28x EBITDA, liquidity is USD 965.9 million and the first maturity is June 2031, so near-term default and refinancing risk are low. Capital intensity comes second: capital spending was 1.78% of net sales in 2025 and free cash flow was positive every year, averaging USD 144.03 million, which leaves cash for debt service of USD 28.13 million a year with 5.12 times cover. Third is the cleaner capital structure after June 2026: one drawn instrument, no amortisation and a fixed coupon. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation P1; calculation P2; calculation P5; calculation P7; calculation P17; calculation P22

Weaknesses. Customer and segment concentration comes first: two customers take about 40% of sales and Light Duty earns 91.57% of segment profit, so one account decision reaches most of the cash flow. The receivable programs come second: USD 970.9 million of funding outside reported debt equals liquidity and costs more than the notes. Third is margin volatility from tariff timing, with Light Duty margin at 12.80% in 2023, 20.53% in 2025 and 18.5% in the latest quarter. Fourth is distribution pace: buybacks took 83.66% of free cash flow excluding refunds in 2026 with the governing limits unknown. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation P10; calculation P12; calculation P15; calculation P16; calculation P19

cells.text: No sponsor, parent or controlling holder is stated. Steven L. Berman and his family beneficially owned about 13% of the common stock at 2026-02-24 (about 15% at 2024-12-31 and about 16% at 2023-12-31) and could influence shareholder votes. 321 holders of record at 2026-02-24; 29,494,032 shares outstanding at 2026-10-22. The beneficial ownership table sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

A 1990 agreement, restated in 2006, gives Berman family holders and family trusts rights of first refusal over each other's shares; the company has agreed to use best efforts to register a deceased holder's shares, at the estate's expense.

Eight directors signed the 2025 annual report on 2026-02-27, including the chief executive officer and the Non-Executive Chairman. By 2026-05-04 the chief executive officer is styled Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer, and the third-quarter report lists Mr. Berman as a Director. Segment presidents were replaced between 2025-05 and 2026-01.

David M. Hession was Chief Financial Officer at 2026-02-27 with Charles W. Rayfield as designate; Mr. Rayfield signed the reports of 2026-05-04, 2026-08-04 and 2026-10-27 as Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer.

USD 3.59 million paid in 2025 under leases and service agreements with entities tied to the Chairman and the former head of Specialty Vehicle (calculation N10); aggregate purchases of USD 24.8 million in 2025 from a supplier joint venture and two minority-owned suppliers, whose ownership percentages are not stated; equity-method investments were carried at USD 12.3 million.
KPMG LLP, Philadelphia, auditor since 2002; unqualified opinions on the 2025 statements and on internal control over financial reporting, with one critical audit matter.

USD 450.0 million 6.25% senior notes due 2034-06-16 (guaranteed by wholly owned subsidiaries that guarantee the credit agreement; security not stated); USD 800.0 million revolver due 2031-06-16, undrawn, secured on substantially all personal property and assets of the company and its material wholly owned domestic subsidiaries, with USD 1.1 million of letters of credit and USD 798.9 million available.

Secured net leverage of not more than 3.50x (4.00x for four fiscal quarters after certain acquisitions) and interest coverage of not less than 2.00x; the issuer reports no ratio value and the definitions are not supplied. The company was not in default at 2026-09-26.
No cash dividend is paid or expected. Repurchase authorisation of USD 500.0 million for 2025 to 2027, of which USD 348.3 million remained at 2026-09-26.
Management language: a key component of strategy is growth through acquisitions, and the company is dedicated to developing the heavy-duty and specialty vehicle sectors.
No agency rating or market quote is stated in the supplied documents; the senior notes had a Level 2 fair value of USD 435.4 million at 2026-09-26.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: In June 2026 Dorman refinanced its whole debt stack. Amendment No. 3 to the credit agreement, dated 16 June 2026, replaced the USD 600.0 million revolver with a five-year USD 800.0 million revolver due 16 June 2031, guaranteed by the material wholly owned domestic subsidiaries and secured on substantially all their personal property and assets. The company also issued USD 450.0 million of 6.25% senior notes due 16 June 2034 under an indenture of the same date, with interest paid each June and December from December 2026. The proceeds repaid the USD 431.3 million term loan balance with accrued interest, paid advisory fees and went to general corporate purposes. The notes are guaranteed by each existing and future wholly owned subsidiary that guarantees the credit agreement; whether they are secured, who the guarantors are and the revolver margin are not stated. At 26 September 2026 the revolver was undrawn, letters of credit were USD 1.1 million and USD 798.9 million was available. The maintenance covenants are secured net leverage of 3.50x, rising to 4.00x for four quarters after certain acquisitions, and interest coverage of 2.00x. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-27_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 32; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 85

The last large transaction was the 4 October 2022 purchase of SuperATV, a powersports aftermarket supplier, for USD 509.8 million net of USD 6.8 million of cash acquired, with an earn-out of up to USD 100.0 million tied to 2023 and 2024 revenue and gross margin targets. It was funded in cash through a refinancing of the existing credit facility, which brought a USD 500.0 million term loan and a USD 600.0 million revolver. The earn-out carried no liability at the end of 2023 or 2024, and the maximum remaining contingent payment across acquisitions fell from USD 102.0 million in the 2024 annual report to USD 2.0 million in the 2025 report. Purchase accounting assigned USD 247.5 million to goodwill and USD 157.5 million to identifiable intangibles. In 2026 the company paid USD 4.5 million for a business in the third quarter and reported a USD 1.5 million bargain purchase gain, and it sold an investment in the second quarter for USD 7.2 million; the target and the investment are not named. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 85, 86, 95; 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 91; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 28; 10-Q_2026-06-27_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 29; EX99.1_2026-09-26_dorm_dorm-20260926xexx991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation N23

Capital returns are by repurchase only. The board authorised up to USD 500.0 million of repurchases from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027, and USD 348.3 million remained at 26 September 2026. Cash spent on repurchases was USD 15.7 million in 2023, USD 80.8 million in 2024, USD 40.6 million in 2025 and USD 113.8 million in nine months 2026. In December 2023 the Colmar headquarters facility, which the company leased from an entity tied to the Chairman's family, was sold to a third party subject to the company's lease; the seller and the proceeds are not stated, and the supplied cash flow statements show no sale proceeds to the company. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 48, 73, 100; 10-K_2024-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 70, 78; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 12, 30; calculation N12; calculation N16

A major 2026 item outside financing is the tariff refund. After the Supreme Court ruling of 20 February 2026 and the March 2026 Court of International Trade order, Dorman recorded USD 98.1 million of refunds in nine months 2026, with USD 2.1 million still receivable at 26 September 2026, and received USD 99.7 million in cash including interest. Section 122 tariffs expired on 24 July 2026 and Section 301 tariffs took effect; the company excludes tariff changes after 26 October 2026 from its guidance. The third-quarter report has no subsequent-events note, and no supplied document is dated after 27 October 2026. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 20, 28, 32; EX99.1_2026-09-26_dorm_dorm-20260926xexx991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Dorman Products, Inc. as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics from the supplied annual reports, quarterly reports and earnings releases to the quarter ended 2026-09-26. Statements are in USD thousands and the money tables in US$m.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage is low and the maturity ladder is long, so the balance sheet puts little near-term pressure on creditors: total debt was 1.28x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 26 September 2026 and the only drawn debt, the senior notes, falls due in 2034.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three qualifications matter. EBITDA is derived because the issuer reports none, and it includes a USD 56.7 million goodwill impairment, so leverage excluding it would be 1.10x. Customer-sponsored receivable sales are a debt-like funding source of USD 970.9 million outside the balance sheet; adding them to debt puts leverage near 3.57x on EBITDA before factoring costs. The senior notes have paid no coupon yet, so last-twelve-months cash interest understates the run rate, and whether the notes are secured is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K81; calculation K84; calculation K93; calculation K94; 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 26; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt to EBITDA fell from 2.14x at the end of fiscal 2023 to 1.38x at the end of fiscal 2024 and 1.24x at the end of fiscal 2025, and was 1.28x on a last-twelve-months basis at 26 September 2026; net debt to EBITDA moved from 2.00x to 1.21x, 1.10x and 0.79x. Carrying-value debt fell from USD 575.6 million to USD 440.7 million, while EBITDA rose from USD 269.5 million to USD 355.3 million and then slipped to USD 344.8 million on a last-twelve-months basis; that figure still carries the goodwill impairment of the fourth quarter of 2025. Interest cover on cash interest paid rose from 5.44x to 17.49x, but the last-twelve-months denominator holds no coupon on the senior notes, which first pay in December 2026. The notes carry a fixed 6.25% on USD 450.0 million, an annual coupon of USD 28.1 million, against a floating rate of 5.07% on the term loan at the end of 2025, so cash interest will step up although debt is unchanged; last-twelve-months EBITDA covers that coupon 12.26x. The creditor consequence is a comfortable cushion that the derived EBITDA and the coupon step both qualify.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K62; calculation K77; calculation K79; calculation K85; calculation K86; 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 71, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow was USD 208.8 million in fiscal 2023, USD 231.0 million in fiscal 2024 and USD 113.6 million in fiscal 2025, when inventories absorbed USD 250.4 million of cash to meet customer demand and pay higher tariffs; after USD 38.0 million of capital expenditure, free cash flow converted only 0.21 of EBITDA. In the nine months to 26 September 2026 operating cash flow rebounded to USD 260.9 million as inventories released USD 177.6 million and USD 99.7 million of tariff refunds and related interest were received, so last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 269.2 million (conversion 0.78) rests on an inventory unwind and refunds that may not repeat. The credit implication is that cash generation is lumpy and tariff-dependent: net debt fell by USD 116.8 million between the end of 2025 and 26 September 2026 even after USD 113.8 million of share repurchases, which shows how much cash management can return to shareholders.

fields.value: Basis: calculation K56; calculation K57; calculation K92; 10-K_2024-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-Q_2026-03-28_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4; 10-Q_2026-06-27_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: At 26 September 2026 cash was USD 167.0 million and USD 798.9 million of the USD 800.0 million revolver was available after USD 1.1 million of letters of credit, for liquidity of USD 965.9 million against total debt of USD 440.7 million. Drawn debt is the senior notes alone, due in 2034; the revolver matures in 2031 and is undrawn, and the term loan that was due in October 2027 under the old agreement was repaid in June 2026. The credit implication is that no principal falls due before 2031, so refinancing is not the near-term risk; the exposure lies in the working-capital programs below and in covenant terms that are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K95; calculation K87; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 7, 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 62, 85

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer-sponsored programs let the company sell receivables without recourse: USD 1,387.8 million were sold in fiscal 2025, 65.15% of net sales, and USD 843.6 million in the nine months to 26 September 2026, 51.59% of net sales and 18.1% less than a year earlier, at a cost of USD 36.1 million recorded in selling, general, and administrative expenses. At 26 September 2026 USD 970.9 million of additional receivables would otherwise have been outstanding. The programs are run by financial institutions for customers, can be modified or terminated, and are priced off Term SOFR, so a withdrawal would move receivables back onto the balance sheet while higher tariff payments are made before the goods are sold; the USD 970.9 million is about equal to total liquidity of USD 965.9 million. Counting the receivables as debt-like funding gives 3.57x on EBITDA before factoring costs (Analyst Judgement); the reported ratios exclude them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K84; calculation K90; calculation K91; calculation K94; 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 62; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 25, 26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tariff refunds are the main one-off. After the Supreme Court ruling of 20 February 2026, which the fiscal 2025 report records as a subsequent event, the company recorded refunds of USD 98.1 million in 2026, of which USD 2.1 million was still receivable at 26 September 2026, and received USD 99.7 million in cash including interest; the second-quarter release shows a USD 44.4 million benefit to second-quarter gross profit and USD 11.3 million to six-month gross profit. These are one event in different roles, kept together in the definition conflict register. Period EBITDA is not adjusted for them because the issuer states no adjusted measure, so second-quarter and nine-month earnings and operating cash flow are flattered and last-twelve-months coverage should be read with that in mind. No event after 26 September 2026 that changes net debt is stated in the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Four points qualify every ratio. EBITDA is derived as income from operations plus depreciation and amortization because the issuer reports none, and the annual figures include accretion in depreciation. Fiscal 2022 was a 53-week year, so growth in fiscal 2023 compares unlike lengths. The first-quarter report prints other income with a negative sign and the third-quarter report separates interest expense from interest income; both were restated to one basis and tie to the printed totals. The covenant tests, secured net leverage not above 3.50x and interest coverage not below 2.00x, are summarised without their definitions, so no headroom is stated and none can be inferred from the ratios in this report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business, ownership, governance and transaction fact review of Dorman Products, Inc. (DORM) as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: what the company does, who owns and runs it, what it has done with debt and equity, and how those facts reach creditors, from the supplied annual reports, quarterly reports and earnings releases to the quarter ended 2026-09-26. The company has no sponsor, so the sponsor and governance work is read as a public-company, shareholder-return and related-party review.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external source was used; every statement comes from the eight supplied files.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dorman is a public aftermarket parts supplier with no sponsor, parent or dividend, so creditors face business concentration and discretionary buyback risk rather than owner extraction, which supports a medium governance risk level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two customers took about 40% of 2025 net sales, all within Light Duty, which supplied 79.43% of sales and 91.57% of segment profit. Repurchases reached USD 113.8 million in nine months 2026, yet the executed financing documents that would show how much the company may distribute were not supplied. All three segment heads and the finance chief changed between February 2025 and May 2026, and the leases with related parties expire in 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 43, 47, 95; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 28; calculation N1; calculation N2; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership risk is low because there is no sponsor, parent or controlling holder, but the Chairman's family stake is influential and shrinking. The family beneficially owned about 13% of the common stock in February 2026, against about 15% a year earlier and about 16% at the end of 2023, and the company itself says the stake lets the family influence board elections and delay a change in control. A sale plan adopted in September 2026 covers 0.66% of shares outstanding, so the consequence for creditors is the absence of a fund exit clock, not a sign of extraction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 95; 10-K_2024-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 99; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 31; calculation N15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns are the main discretionary drain on creditor cash, and the company's capacity to make them cannot be tested. No dividend is paid, but repurchases cost USD 113.8 million in nine months 2026, which is 48.28% of operating cash flow less capital spending and 83.66% once USD 99.7 million of tariff refunds and related interest, which came from one court ruling, is removed; USD 348.3 million of the USD 500.0 million authorisation remains to the end of 2027. Willingness to return cash is documented, while the limits that the new credit agreement and indenture place on it are not, so creditors cannot say how much of the remaining authorisation is permitted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 5, 12, 28, 30; calculation N12; calculation N13; calculation N16; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is concentrated in one segment and two customers. Light Duty supplied 79.43% of 2025 sales and 91.57% of segment profit, and the two customers that each exceeded 10% of sales took about 40% of the company total, about half of Light Duty sales. Their contracts typically carry no purchase commitment, the company records that large customers press for lower prices, longer payment terms and higher rebates, and customer credit provisions were USD 404.2 million in 2025, 18.97% of net sales. The four largest customers also owed 78% of receivables at the end of 2025. A loss or repricing at either large account would hit the segment that earns almost all segment profit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 21, 22, 34, 79, 80, 86, 95, 111; calculation N1; calculation N2; calculation N5; calculation N17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Heavy Duty and Specialty Vehicle give little earnings cushion, and the acquisition that built Specialty Vehicle has so far returned little against its price. Heavy Duty made USD 5.11 million of segment profit on USD 232.59 million of 2025 sales, wrote off all USD 56.71 million of its goodwill in the fourth quarter of 2025 and reported a small segment loss in the third quarter of 2026. Specialty Vehicle, bought in 2022 for USD 509.8 million, earned USD 26.85 million of segment profit in 2025, equal to 5.27% of that price and 15.08% below 2023, and the earn-out of up to USD 100.0 million carried no liability at the end of 2023 or 2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 59, 83, 86–87; 10-K_2024-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 85, 95; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation N2; calculation N7; calculation N8; calculation N9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Related-party leakage is small in cash, and the continuity risks are the 2027 lease expiries and the turnover in senior roles. Rent and services paid to entities tied to the Chairman and to the former head of Specialty Vehicle were USD 3.59 million in 2025, 0.17% of net sales. The leases for the Madison and Shreveport sites that house specialty vehicle manufacturing and warehousing, and the Chairman-related Lewisberry lease, all expire in 2027 with renewal terms not stated. The three segment heads and the finance chief changed between February 2025 and May 2026, and the Chairman title moved to the chief executive, so board independence, which the missing proxy statement leaves unestablished, becomes a monitoring point.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 42, 43, 47, 65, 88; 10-K_2024-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-03-28_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX99.1_2026-03-28_dorm_dorm-20260328xexx991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation N10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financing is now long-dated and plain, but ranking and distribution capacity rest on documents that were not supplied. The June 2026 refinancing replaced a USD 600.0 million revolver and a term loan due October 2027 with an undrawn USD 800.0 million secured revolver due June 2031 and USD 450.0 million of 6.25% senior notes due June 2034, guaranteed by the same subsidiaries that guarantee the credit agreement; whether the notes are secured is not stated. Management calls acquisitions a key part of strategy, and the secured net leverage covenant of 3.50x rises to 4.00x for four quarters after certain acquisitions, so a large debt-funded purchase is the event to watch.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 16, 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-Q_2026-06-27_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 32; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality supports monitoring of operations. The auditor has served since 2002 and gave unqualified opinions on the statements and on internal control, and its one critical audit matter was the accrual for customer credits, USD 197.4 million at the end of 2025, the reserve most sensitive to customer behaviour.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a lower risk level is that nothing in the eight documents shows extraction or creditor-adverse conduct. There is no dividend, no management, monitoring or advisory fee to a shareholder, and no waiver, forbearance or exchange offer; the refinancing lengthened maturities, and the revolver was undrawn with USD 798.9 million available at the end of September 2026. Repurchases were paid from operating cash flow, since cash rose by USD 117.6 million over the nine months after USD 113.8 million of buybacks, and the share count fell by 2.69% between the end of 2025 and the end of September 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4, 5, 26, 28; calculation N20; calculation N21; calculation N24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Evidence for a higher level is the pace and the dependence: repurchases absorbed most of free cash flow once the refund effect is removed, two customers hold about 40% of sales, and the financial institutions that run the customer-sponsored receivable programs can modify or terminate them. The view would move to low if the executed documents show binding limits on restricted payments and the proxy statement shows an independent majority board. It would move to high if repurchases keep running above underlying free cash flow after the refunds end, if the revolver is drawn to fund them, or if either large customer cuts volume or a receivable program is withdrawn.

fields.value: - The executed credit agreement and indenture were not supplied, so the shareholder-return conclusion cannot be tested against restricted-payment limits; tight limits would lower the risk level and loose ones would raise it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 proxy statement was not supplied, so board independence, committee membership, compensation design and the beneficial ownership table are not established, and the finding that the Chairman's family holds the only large stake rests on one risk factor in the annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The dates and reasons for the Chairman, finance chief and segment-head changes are not stated, so the continuity finding cannot say whether the turnover was planned succession or disruption.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer names, contract terms and the identity of the customers behind the receivable programs are not disclosed, so the concentration finding cannot size the loss from a single account or say how much funding would leave with it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Segment profit excludes acquisition amortisation and special charges, so the 5.27% return on the Specialty Vehicle purchase price is a segment-level indication, not a return on invested capital.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Statements that the company is a leading supplier and its USD 165 billion market estimate are management language that no supplied source verifies, so the business description rests on reported results, not on those claims.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In June 2026 Dorman refinanced its whole debt stack. Amendment No. 3 to the credit agreement, dated 16 June 2026, replaced the USD 600.0 million revolver with a five-year USD 800.0 million revolver due 16 June 2031, guaranteed by the material wholly owned domestic subsidiaries and secured on substantially all their personal property and assets. The company also issued USD 450.0 million of 6.25% senior notes due 16 June 2034 under an indenture of the same date, with interest paid each June and December from December 2026. The proceeds repaid the USD 431.3 million term loan balance with accrued interest, paid advisory fees and went to general corporate purposes. The notes are guaranteed by each existing and future wholly owned subsidiary that guarantees the credit agreement; whether they are secured, who the guarantors are and the revolver margin are not stated. At 26 September 2026 the revolver was undrawn, letters of credit were USD 1.1 million and USD 798.9 million was available. The maintenance covenants are secured net leverage of 3.50x, rising to 4.00x for four quarters after certain acquisitions, and interest coverage of 2.00x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The last large transaction was the 4 October 2022 purchase of SuperATV, a powersports aftermarket supplier, for USD 509.8 million net of USD 6.8 million of cash acquired, with an earn-out of up to USD 100.0 million tied to 2023 and 2024 revenue and gross margin targets. It was funded in cash through a refinancing of the existing credit facility, which brought a USD 500.0 million term loan and a USD 600.0 million revolver. The earn-out carried no liability at the end of 2023 or 2024, and the maximum remaining contingent payment across acquisitions fell from USD 102.0 million in the 2024 annual report to USD 2.0 million in the 2025 report. Purchase accounting assigned USD 247.5 million to goodwill and USD 157.5 million to identifiable intangibles. In 2026 the company paid USD 4.5 million for a business in the third quarter and reported a USD 1.5 million bargain purchase gain, and it sold an investment in the second quarter for USD 7.2 million; the target and the investment are not named.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital returns are by repurchase only. The board authorised up to USD 500.0 million of repurchases from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027, and USD 348.3 million remained at 26 September 2026. Cash spent on repurchases was USD 15.7 million in 2023, USD 80.8 million in 2024, USD 40.6 million in 2025 and USD 113.8 million in nine months 2026. In December 2023 the Colmar headquarters facility, which the company leased from an entity tied to the Chairman's family, was sold to a third party subject to the company's lease; the seller and the proceeds are not stated, and the supplied cash flow statements show no sale proceeds to the company.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 48, 73, 100; 10-K_2024-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 70, 78; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 12, 30; calculation N12; calculation N16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A major 2026 item outside financing is the tariff refund. After the Supreme Court ruling of 20 February 2026 and the March 2026 Court of International Trade order, Dorman recorded USD 98.1 million of refunds in nine months 2026, with USD 2.1 million still receivable at 26 September 2026, and received USD 99.7 million in cash including interest. Section 122 tariffs expired on 24 July 2026 and Section 301 tariffs took effect; the company excludes tariff changes after 26 October 2026 from its guidance. The third-quarter report has no subsequent-events note, and no supplied document is dated after 27 October 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Ready with limitations. No external source was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is driven by discretionary share repurchases and by legal capacity that cannot be tested, because buybacks compete with debt reduction and the documents that limit them were not supplied, which implies moderate pressure on creditor cash and a monitoring need rather than a finding of extraction. Countervailing evidence is the absence of any dividend, sponsor fee, waiver or exchange offer in the documents, an undrawn revolver and a refinancing that lengthened maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Dorman presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is the growth of repurchases to USD 113.8 million in nine months 2026, which matters because it uses free cash flow that the 2026 tariff refunds inflated, and implies that creditors should track buyback pace against cash generation. Countervailing evidence is the family stake of about 13% with no sponsor, no dividend and no creditor-adverse transaction. Further analysis requires the executed credit agreement and indenture, the 2026 proxy statement and the dates of the leadership changes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance review completed with limitations. Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. Key gaps: executed financing documents, proxy statement, dates of leadership changes, customer terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit review of Dorman Products, Inc. (DORM) as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the integrated credit view built from the supplied annual reports, quarterly reports and earnings releases to the quarter ended 2026-09-26, with the financial figures taken from Financial foundation and the ownership, governance and transaction facts from Business & governance. No legal, covenant-capacity, recovery, relative-value or sizing conclusion is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external source was used; every statement comes from the eight supplied files and the three earlier reviews.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dorman is a conservatively financed auto-parts supplier whose 1.28x total debt to EBITDA, USD 965.9 million of liquidity and first maturity in 2031 give creditors a strong cushion, constrained mainly by customer concentration and off-balance-sheet receivable funding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation P1; calculation P2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The two weak points are linked: two customers took about 40% of sales, and USD 970.9 million of receivables sit in customer-sponsored programs, almost equal to total liquidity. Earnings swing with tariff timing, so cash-flow durability is adequate rather than strong: free cash flow averaged USD 144.03 million over 2023 to 2025 against USD 28.13 million of annual note interest. The medium governance risk from Business & governance stands, and only covenant headroom and ranking depend on documents that were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation P4; calculation P5; calculation P10; calculation P15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage, liquidity and maturities are the strongest part of the credit. Total debt of USD 440.7 million is 1.28x last-twelve-months EBITDA and net debt of USD 273.7 million is 0.79x; EBITDA is derived because the issuer reports none, and excluding the USD 56.7 million Heavy Duty goodwill write-off leverage is 1.10x. Liquidity is USD 965.9 million, being cash of USD 167.0 million and USD 798.9 million of undrawn revolver, and the first maturity is the revolver in June 2031, followed by the USD 450.0 million notes in June 2034. The creditor consequence is that refinancing is not a near-term risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 26; calculation P1; calculation P2; calculation P3; calculation P22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash-flow durability is adequate, not strong, because free cash flow is volatile and the latest figure is flattered. Free cash flow was USD 191.6 million in 2024, USD 75.7 million in 2025 after a USD 250.4 million inventory build, and USD 269.2 million over the last twelve months, which includes USD 99.7 million of tariff refunds and a USD 177.6 million inventory release in nine months. Through the three years 2023 to 2025 it averaged USD 144.03 million, 44% of EBITDA, and covered the annual coupon of USD 28.13 million 5.12 times; excluding the refunds, last-twelve-months conversion is 49%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 28; calculation P5; calculation P6; calculation P7; calculation P8; calculation P9; calculation P22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business diversification is the weakest dimension. Light Duty is 79.43% of sales and 91.57% of segment profit, two customers take about 40% of sales and the four largest owe 78% of receivables, so a price or volume decision by one account reaches the segment that carries the debt. Heavy Duty earns 1.35% of segment profit and Specialty Vehicle, bought for USD 509.8 million, adds little cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 79, 80, 95; calculation P15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The receivable programs are a second dependency of the same size as liquidity. USD 970.9 million of receivables would otherwise be outstanding, which is 1.01 times liquidity, and the financial institutions that run the programs can modify or terminate them; counting the receivables as debt-like funding lifts leverage to 3.57x. The programs also cost USD 50.7 million over the last twelve months, 1.80 times the annual note coupon, so they are a larger financing cost than the notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation P10; calculation P11; calculation P12; calculation P22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin stability is average because tariff timing moves earnings by several percentage points. The Light Duty segment margin rose from 12.80% in 2023 to 20.53% in 2025 and was 18.5% in the third quarter of 2026 against 23.7% a year earlier, while the group gross margin fell by 500 bp to 39.4%, because tariff costs are capitalised in inventory and price rises lead cost recognition. Earnings therefore depend on how fast the company passes tariff costs to customers who press for lower prices.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 20, 21, 23; calculation P16; calculation P17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing capacity is strong but its documents are not in the set. The June 2026 refinancing placed USD 450.0 million of 6.25% notes and extended the revolver to 2031, and the notes had a fair value of 96.76% of principal at the end of September 2026. Ranking, the security of the notes and covenant headroom are not established, so the view rests on maturity dates, liquidity and leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 12, 26; calculation P14; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the swing factor and is rated average. There is no dividend, but repurchases of USD 113.8 million in nine months 2026 took 83.66% of free cash flow excluding refunds, with USD 348.3 million of authorisation left, and the limits that the new documents place on them are not known. Business & governance rates the sponsor and governance risk medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 12, 28; calculation P19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is a tariff-led margin squeeze on Light Duty with pressure on the receivable programs. If the Light Duty margin fell back to its 2023 level of 12.80%, segment profit would fall by USD 130.74 million, EBITDA would be USD 214.05 million and total debt to EBITDA 2.06x, still below the 2.14x of 2023 and with 7.61 times coverage of the coupon; the larger risk is a withdrawal of the programs, which would need slightly more than all of today's liquidity. Both are bounds, not forecasts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation P2; calculation P10; calculation P18; calculation P22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a strong cushion is that the headline ratios are flattered and part of the liquidity rests on programs that third-party institutions run for customers. EBITDA is derived, the latest free cash flow includes tariff refunds and an inventory release, the receivable programs equal liquidity, and the revolver's availability of USD 798.9 million is only as good as the borrowing conditions and covenants that were not supplied. Repurchases at the 2026 pace would also use most of the underlying free cash flow, which is why the financial policy dimension is only average.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation P2; calculation P8; calculation P10; calculation P19; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Evidence the other way is that every test applied here leaves headroom: leverage stays near 2x even with the 2023 margin, coupon cover is 7.61 times in that case, the first maturity is 2031 and capital spending is only 1.78% of net sales. The view would weaken if gross margin fell below 39.4% for a second quarter, if the revolver were drawn to fund repurchases or a large acquisition, if either large customer cut orders, or if receivables sold fell sharply. It would strengthen if the executed documents show wide covenant headroom and a bar on large distributions, or if the customer base broadened.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation P17; calculation P18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement and indenture were not supplied, so covenant headroom, the ranking of the senior notes and their security are not established, and the strong refinancing assessment rests on maturity dates, liquidity and leverage alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - EBITDA is derived by the financial review because the issuer reports none, and it carries the goodwill write-off and the 2026 tariff effects, so each leverage and coverage figure here would move if a covenant or issuer-adjusted EBITDA were supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No rating, market quotation or peer set is supplied, so the labels strong, average and weak describe the company against its own history and its sources, not against comparable issuers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The payment terms and notice periods of the receivable programs are not disclosed, so the time over which USD 970.9 million could return to the balance sheet is not established and the liquidity downside is a bound, not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside figures take the 2023 Light Duty margin as the stress and treat the change in segment profit as the change in EBITDA, with no management forecast or bridge to test them against, so they show scale rather than probability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Leverage and liquidity come first: total debt of USD 440.7 million is 1.28x EBITDA, liquidity is USD 965.9 million and the first maturity is June 2031, so near-term default and refinancing risk are low. Capital intensity comes second: capital spending was 1.78% of net sales in 2025 and free cash flow was positive every year, averaging USD 144.03 million, which leaves cash for debt service of USD 28.13 million a year with 5.12 times cover. Third is the cleaner capital structure after June 2026: one drawn instrument, no amortisation and a fixed coupon.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation P1; calculation P2; calculation P5; calculation P7; calculation P17; calculation P22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Customer and segment concentration comes first: two customers take about 40% of sales and Light Duty earns 91.57% of segment profit, so one account decision reaches most of the cash flow. The receivable programs come second: USD 970.9 million of funding outside reported debt equals liquidity and costs more than the notes. Third is margin volatility from tariff timing, with Light Duty margin at 12.80% in 2023, 20.53% in 2025 and 18.5% in the latest quarter. Fourth is distribution pace: buybacks took 83.66% of free cash flow excluding refunds in 2026 with the governing limits unknown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation P10; calculation P12; calculation P15; calculation P16; calculation P19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dorman supplies replacement and upgrade parts to the motor vehicle aftermarket and sells mostly through retailers, dealers and distributors in North America. About 76% of 2025 products carried owned brands, most light-duty products are made by third parties and most specialty vehicle products are made in the company's own plants, so the company carries design and sourcing risk more than factory risk. Most sales are repair parts, which the company describes as less cyclical, and demand follows vehicle age and use: vehicles in operation reached 302.7 million with an average age of 12.9 years. For creditors this means demand is steady but visibility is short, because customer agreements typically carry no purchase commitment and revenue is recognised on purchase orders of one year or less.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dorman is a public company with no sponsor or parent. The Chairman's family held about 13% of the common stock in February 2026, down from about 16% at the end of 2023, and it sells under planned sale programs, so there is no fund exit clock and no extraction is shown in the documents. The borrower group is the consolidated company: the revolver is guaranteed and secured by the material wholly owned domestic subsidiaries and the senior notes carry the same subsidiary guarantees, with the notes' security and the guarantor names not established. Financial policy shows no dividend, USD 113.8 million of repurchases in nine months 2026 and a stated appetite for acquisitions, with a leverage covenant that allows 4.00x for four quarters after certain acquisitions. Related-party rent of USD 3.59 million in 2025 is small. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is transactional, concentrated and partly price-led. Net sales rose 6.03% in 2025 on tariff-related pricing, early-year demand and new products, and 2.68% in nine months 2026 on pricing partly offset by lower volume, while third-quarter growth of 3.3% came from Light Duty volume and business wins net of price decreases in some categories. The company has some pass-through, because it raised prices as tariffs rose, but the pass-through lags cost recognition and its large customers push for lower prices, longer terms and higher rebates, with customer credit provisions of USD 404.2 million in 2025. The credit consequence is that revenue is predictable at the level of the repair category and unpredictable at the level of price and account.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 59, 60; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 22, 23; calculation P20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended only as fast as tariff costs are passed on. Gross margin was 42.14% in 2025 and fell 500 bp to 39.4% in the third quarter of 2026 as higher-cost inventory reached cost of goods; about 77% of purchases come from outside the United States and about 38% from China, and tariffs are capitalised in inventory, which delays the hit. Selling, general and administrative expense is 25.42% of sales including factoring costs of 2.74% of sales, which are priced off Term SOFR, so operating leverage is moderate and a fall in sales would not be offset by cost cuts quickly. The company's levers are price increases, supplier diversification and automation, which it describes as mitigation without a stated size.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 57, 58; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 20, 21; calculation P17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low and conversion is driven by working capital. Capital spending was 1.78% of net sales in 2025, operating leases call for USD 30.0 million of payments within twelve months, cash taxes were USD 68.6 million in 2025 and cash interest USD 27.4 million, which will rise to the note coupon of USD 28.13 million. Conversion fell to 0.21 of EBITDA in 2025 when inventory absorbed USD 250.4 million and rebounded in 2026 as inventory released USD 177.6 million and tariff refunds arrived; the three-year average of 0.44 is the better guide to what is available for debt service. Capital spending can be cut, but at 1.78% of sales it offers little cash relief.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 72, 89; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation P6; calculation P9; calculation P17; calculation P20; calculation P22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is high. The company names a broad field including Standard Motor Products, Tenneco, Bosch, Gates and ACDelco, original equipment makers selling through dealers and some customers whose private labels compete, which pressures price and supports the customers' demands for rebates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is moderate: the catalogue of about 144,000 parts and the limited shelf space at retailers protect incumbents, but the company says it cannot assure that entrants will not appear and notes that e-commerce growth and artificial intelligence may help competitors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of substitutes is moderate: original equipment parts through dealers compete directly, and better vehicle quality and longer manufacturer warranties could cut part replacement frequency over time.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is the most important force. Two customers take about 40% of sales and the four largest owe 78% of receivables, they carry no purchase commitments, and they can buy direct from suppliers, so pricing and terms are set largely by them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is low to moderate: more than 400 suppliers and none above 10% of purchases limit single-source risk, and the exposure that matters is tariff and currency terms on imports, not supplier pricing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors are material through tariffs. The Supreme Court ruling of 20 February 2026 opened refunds of USD 98.1 million, short-term Section 122 tariffs expired on 24 July 2026 and new Section 301 tariffs took effect, and the company excludes tariff changes after 26 October 2026 from its guidance. Economic factors matter through Term SOFR, which sets the cost of the receivable programs at about USD 11.3 million a year per percentage point on 2025 volumes, and through fuel prices and miles driven. Technology matters because vehicle electronics and manufacturer limits on repair data could narrow what the company can design. Social factors are not a primary credit driver on the supplied materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 34, 101; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 16, 19, 20; EX99.1_2026-09-26_dorm_dorm-20260926xexx991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation P13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strengths: low leverage and large liquidity; a simple, long-dated debt structure; low capital intensity; owned brands and a wide catalogue; no dividend.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation P1; calculation P2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weaknesses: concentration in Light Duty and two customers; near-zero profit in Heavy Duty after a full goodwill write-off; funding float equal to liquidity; margin swings from tariff timing; unknown limits on buybacks.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Opportunities that could improve credit quality: replacement demand from an ageing vehicle base, new-product wins in Light Duty, and further tariff relief that restores margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Threats that could weaken credit quality: new tariffs that are not passed through, a customer repricing or direct sourcing, curtailment of the receivable programs, and a large debt-funded acquisition or buyback.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scale and market position: average. Net sales of USD 2,173.02 million over the last twelve months are meaningful, but no market share or peer data is supplied and the company's own market estimate implies a share of about 1.3%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation P22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Competitive advantage: average. Owned brands account for about 76% of products and 5,560 new parts were introduced in 2025, but rivals include original equipment makers and customers' private labels and no switching cost is evidenced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Business diversification: weak. Light Duty is 79.43% of sales and 91.57% of segment profit and two customers take about 40% of sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cost and capex flexibility: average. Capital spending is only 1.78% of sales and repurchases are discretionary, but input costs follow tariffs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation P17; 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, page 57

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin stability: average. The Light Duty margin ranged from 12.80% to 20.53% in two years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow stability: average. Free cash flow was positive every year but ranged from USD 75.7 million to USD 269.2 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation P5; calculation P22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ability to refinance or access capital markets: strong. USD 450.0 million of notes were placed in June 2026, no maturity falls before June 2031 and leverage is 1.28x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity position: strong. Liquidity is USD 965.9 million, with USD 798.9 million of undrawn revolver, though the receivable programs are a comparable amount of funding outside debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation P2; calculation P10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy and governance: average. There is no dividend and no extraction is shown in the documents, but repurchases are rising and legal capacity is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Short term, over 12 to 24 months, the guidance narrowed to net sales growth of 2% to 3% and adjusted diluted EPS of USD 8.50 to USD 8.70, which is 2% to 4% below 2025, because tariff costs have caught up with the pricing taken in 2025; a first coupon in December 2026 lifts cash interest by about USD 8.41 million a year over the last twelve months. Tailwinds are new products and business wins in Light Duty and an ageing vehicle base; headwinds are Section 301 tariffs, higher rates on the programs and a refund benefit that will not repeat.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-26_dorm_dorm-20260926xexx991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 20, 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation P4; calculation P21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Medium term, over three to five years, the debt profile is supportive, with a revolver due 2031 and notes due 2034, and the repurchase authorisation ends in 2027. The sector backdrop of 302.7 million vehicles with an average age of 12.9 years supports demand, while better vehicle quality and OEM control of repair data are the structural headwinds; the related-party site leases that expire in 2027 are a company-specific point to watch.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 28, 43, 100; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation P21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario starts with a tariff increase that is not passed through quickly, together with a repricing demand from a large Light Duty customer. The first operational break is gross margin: it already fell by 500 bp in the third quarter of 2026, and if the Light Duty margin returned to its 2023 level of 12.80% segment profit would fall by USD 130.74 million. EBITDA would then be USD 214.05 million, total debt to EBITDA 2.06x and net debt to EBITDA 1.28x, with the coupon covered 7.61 times, so leverage stays below the 2.14x of fiscal 2023. Free cash flow would fall, as it did to USD 75.7 million in 2025 when inventory absorbed cash, and the pressure would then fall on funding: if the institutions that run the receivable programs curtailed them, USD 970.9 million of receivables would return to the balance sheet against liquidity of USD 965.9 million. Management levers are stopping repurchases, which were USD 113.8 million in nine months 2026, releasing inventory, as USD 177.6 million was released in 2026, raising prices and cutting capital spending, which is only 1.78% of sales. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in the margin case and in a gradual program run-off, while an abrupt loss of all programs with no replacement would exhaust liquidity; the observable triggers are third-quarter-type margin readings, a revolver draw and a fall in receivables sold. The ratios are illustrative bounds, and covenant headroom is not calculable because the definitions were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-26_dorm.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 26; calculation P2; calculation P9; calculation P10; calculation P17; calculation P18; calculation P22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Dorman presents an adequate business profile supported by owned brands, light capital intensity and a repair-led demand base, but credit quality is constrained by concentration in one segment and two customers, tariff-driven margin swings and reliance on customer-sponsored receivable funding. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow averaged USD 144.03 million over three years against a coupon of USD 28.13 million but swung between USD 75.7 million and USD 269.2 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the continued availability of the USD 800.0 million revolver, whose borrowing conditions and covenants were not supplied, and on market access that the June 2026 notes issue showed. The financial profile has improved from 2.14x total debt to EBITDA in 2023 to 1.28x. Comparison with typical issuers in the sector is not established because no peer set was supplied. The primary downside path is a tariff-led margin squeeze on Light Duty together with a withdrawal of receivable programs. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indenture, customer and program terms, and the dates of the leadership changes. Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: concentration of earnings in Light Duty and its two largest customers.
